A '''refueling station''' was single-handedly operated by the [[Bimm (furred species)/Legends|Bimm]] businesswoman [[Sindee]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="DRA" /> Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="Chronology note">{{SW|url=news/the-droids-re-animated-part-1|series=The Droids Re-Animated|text=Part 1|nolive=1}} establishes that [[Sindee]] acquired [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] approximately fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of {{Film|IV}}, which are dated to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> she acquired the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] when they were dumped at her [[refueling station]].<ref name="DRA" /> To help her pass the time, the Bimm taught R2-D2 to play a competent game of [[Dejarik/Legends|dejarik]] [[Holochess/Legends|holo-chess]].<ref name="Rogues">{{SWRadio|Rogues, Rebels and Robots}}</ref> The droids departed when Sindee's [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] addiction led her to lose them in a game of [[Liar's Cut/Legends|Liar's Cut]] to the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Zevel Hortine]].<ref name="DRA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The refueling station was first mentioned in the [[1981]] [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio]] episode "[[Rogues, Rebels and Robots]]."<ref name="Rogues" /> The station was first described in the [[2013]] [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|blog]] article "[[The Droids Re-Animated]]" by [[Rich Handley]] and [[Abel G. Peña]].<ref name="DRA" />
